title: Quiz: Similar Shapes: Area and Volume

questions.stem: Two similar shapes have a length scale factor of $3$. What is the area scale factor?
questions.explanation: The area scale factor is the square of the length scale factor: $3^2 = 9$.

questions.stem: Two similar solids have a length scale factor of $2$. What is the volume scale factor?
questions.explanation: The volume scale factor is the cube of the length scale factor: $2^3 = 8$.

questions.stem: Two similar triangles have areas of $12$ cm$^2$ and $48$ cm$^2$. What is the length scale factor from the smaller to the larger?
questions.explanation: Area scale factor $= \frac{48}{12} = 4$. Length scale factor $= \sqrt{4} = 2$.

questions.stem: Two similar cylinders have heights of $5$ cm and $15$ cm. The surface area of the smaller is $80$ cm$^2$. What is the surface area of the larger?
questions.explanation: Length scale factor $= \frac{15}{5} = 3$. Area scale factor $= 3^2 = 9$. Surface area $= 80 \times 9 = 720$ cm$^2$.

questions.stem: Two similar solids have volumes of $64$ cm$^3$ and $216$ cm$^3$. What is the ratio of their corresponding lengths?
A model car is made at a scale of $1:20$. The real car has a paint area of $8$ m$^2$. What is the paint area of the model?
questions.explanation: Area scale factor $= 20^2 = 400$. Model area $= \frac{8}{400} = 0.02$ m$^2 = 200$ cm$^2$.
